column32:
1. Quite a strange painting. Musicians are shown as if Westerners.
2. Barrel drum shape ambiguity : Shape is like a dholak but hands are in swing like Pakhawaj.
3. Something that looks like Khamancheh
4. In some other corner there is someone with Tambur looking instrument with a probably a singer.

This is pretty non-standard and unusual painting

1. There is only one percussion but we are uncertain whether it is pakhawaj or dholak. It must be pakhawaj looking at the configuration. Nonetheless, it has been marked 1 for pakhawaj and 3 for dholak.
2. A 1800 miniature. Probably a blind copy of existing norms of the miniature. Tambora looks like Sitar but played like tambora, so seems that the artist is just copying from existing formule
3. Though the collection does not mention it to be a Raagmala, configuration looks like it is a raagmala of Vasant

1. Again probably raagmala. But more uncertain than the above.
2. Only Been is depicted.

1. All women. There is no singer.
2. Tambora with Taal indicating person, no Pakhawaj.
3. Distinct 4 pegs tanpura.

1. Ascribed to Rajasthan school (Rajput) but looks like it is Dakkhani. Women are wearing Sakaccha (9Wari).
2. This kind of Image is very much visible in Maratha.
3. Unusual configuration Pakhawaj, Sarangi and tanpura. No singer.
4. Distinct Pakhawaj : Wooden blocks towards the base head. Base head does not have Shyai, treble head has shyai  Full palm stroke

1. Raagmala of Raag Pancham : Deepak raags ragini.
2. Though it probably also shows other 4 raginis. Pancham being the lead?
3. The text starts with "This is the form of all 5 raginis of deepak".
4. In none of the texts, Pancham is a ragini of Deepak So it is doubtful. (Kshemkarn Raagmala, Sangeet damodar and Fakirullah)
5. Interestingly Pakhawaj shyai is shown as half sphere going inside the Pakhawaj head.

1. Same raagmala as above.
2. Raagmala painting of Raag Malav : Deepak's ragini. Again, none of the texts mentions Malav as a ragini of Deepak.
3. Musician's sequence is same Been Tambura Pakhawaj and Kartal.
5. Pakhawaji is left handed.
6. Shyai depicted as above

1.Tambora and singer is the same person.
2. 4 Pegs tanpura.
3. Uncertain about the type. Description says it is some raagmala. But seems not so.

1. Raagmala of Raag Basant/Vasant
2. Men is a dancer.  2 Women are accompanying.
3. Probably all are wearing Gungru. Man is also wearing a Ghungru belt.

1. From Bhagwatpuran hence marked as type as 5.
2. Not a typical scene but musicians are seen in a cornor playing Nei and Naggara/Choughada
1. There is one instrument that is ambiguous. It is either Rabab or bowed kind

1. The instrument other than been looks like either a sehtar or Sitar. Considering how it is hold it is Sitar.
2. Looking at the fingers of other person (One not playing been) it seems that is it not a drone but they are doing music together
